II17A-01.note: North-facing slopes are colder AND lower-UV, so darker beetles there pull the two hypotheses apart in Halloran's favor; requires combining the hypotheses with the last sentence. D is tempting but restates the elevation pattern that 'fits both'; A is the mirror that favors Ide.

II17A-02.note: Local clay at Okrin implies local manufacture, i.e., resettled potters. B is the mirror supporting the trade account; C and D are non-discriminating patterns strikable from the option set's logic alone.

II17A-03.note: Inland bridges remove sea spray, so galvanized > ungalvanized there isolates the acid-cleaning hydrogen. B is the strong trap: it confounds galvanizing with coastal exposure; A supports the consultant; C reverses.

II17A-04.note: To show Sorrin is younger than EVERY southern plain, compare it with the least-cratered (youngest) southern plain, Dunmo (57). C and D show it younger than only one southern plain without covering Dunmo; A compares with a northern plain, irrelevant to the claim.

II17A-05.note: Only 6h and 8h keep peak <20 and trough >4; least frequent of those is 8h. A is within limits but not least frequent; B tempts as 'least frequent' but fails both limits narrowly.

II17A-06.note: Clay at ~85 m: P (22 m) is shallow and S (96 m) is deep, so A contrasts the two aquifers. B is the trap with the bigger gap, but R (78 m) is still above the clay, so both wells are shallow; C and D compare within one aquifer.

II17B-01.note: The board heard only merchant-merchant cases while the herring slump hit everyone, so a merchant-only decline favors Calloway. A fits both accounts (inland towns had neither factor); D favors the herring account.

II17B-02.note: Horns are used in both settings but veterans march only in processions, so equal slowing in seated concerts favors Lindqvist. B favors the archivist; D is tempting but post-1919 also covers the horn adoption, so it does not discriminate (and leans archivist).

II17B-03.note: Carriage charged by weight means cheaper hauling helps heavy grain most, while a price bulletin should help both goods alike. A is the trap: bulletin riders also traveled the turnpikes, so turnpike towns got both; B favors the bulletin; C reverses.

II17B-04.note: For children with books, adding lessons moved +8 to +9. D tempts (lessons-only vs both) but measures the books' contribution; A and C compare against the no-books baseline.

II17B-05.note: Acceptance rate is accepted/submitted: 25% to 50%, and only A gives both figures for landscapes. C tempts by showing accepted rising but omits submissions, so it cannot separate jury receptivity from supply.

II17B-06.note: The 1995 20-29 group are the 2020 45-54 group (same individuals); 38% to 40% shows they kept the vowel. A is the trap: same age bracket but different people (a change across cohorts); B and D are cross-sectional age gaps.
